overall_summary: The channel recently tested family and relationship bond topics (e.g., Mom, Dad, Wife) which massively outperformed the hyper-niche 'self respect' digital-detachment content (getting views up to 1,447 vs 10-40 views). However, core channel branding centers on 'Dil Ki Diary' emotional depth. The winning pattern points toward universally relatable human relational bonds and daily life observations rather than just phone-blocking tropes.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos about Wife, Father, Mother, and general close relationships (e.g., 'पत्नी की ये बात हर पति को समझनी चाहिए' with 1,447 views, 'आज किसी अपने को Call कर लेना' with 287 views) significantly outperformed niche digital self-respect content.
winning_patterns.action: Pivot the emotional storytelling from strictly digital breakup/self-respect tropes to broader, highly universal relationship and family dynamics.

winning_patterns.evidence: Concrete daily life actions or silent sacrifices (e.g., unsaid exhaustion of parents, checking in on someone) drive much higher engagement and views than abstract text-message heartbreak.
winning_patterns.action: Use specific, tactile real-life triggers instead of repeating phone-screen or chat-deletion hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple videos focusing on removing names from shared albums, blocking, muting, or hiding last seen (e.g., 'जब गैलरी की शेयर्ड एलबम से उसका नाम हटाया', 'चैट से उसका नाम अनपिन करते ही') stalled between 0 to 41 views.
weak_patterns.action: Stop using repetitive phone UI and chat-deletion hooks; the audience for this specific narrow sub-niche has saturated or lacks broad appeal.

weak_patterns.evidence: Almost all historical videos have 0 comments, indicating a lack of native conversation-starters in the captions or endings.
weak_patterns.action: Incorporate subtle, conversational prompt questions in the final frame to encourage comments.
